risks.title: Risks & Tradeoffs Requiring Leadership Support
risks.subtitle: Timeline assumes near-perfect execution; here are the gaps and what is being done to address them

rows.working_through: Cross-pod dependencies must be sequenced right: Funding & Metrics, Architecture/tech setup, and Role definitions must land in order.
rows.doing_done: Surfaced and mapped initial dependencies; continuing to sequence them as pods document roadmaps.
rows.needed: Endorse phased approach and accept imperfection and delay as cost of learning.
rows.implication: Operationalization will continue to flex as the pilot proves out the sequence.

rows.working_through: Change absorption: a natural "slow before speed up" period as teams internalize the change.
rows.doing_done: Published role definitions and cards, drafted comms/change plan; planning training, job aids, and a ~2-week ramp with weekly Q&A.
rows.needed: Air cover through the slow-down period and backing to fund coaching and job aids.
rows.implication: Teams operationalize before they are ready and adoption stalls.

rows.working_through: Single-SME reliance: critical knowledge sits with limited individuals with competing priorities.
rows.doing_done: Engaged the key SMEs; continuing to work with them async to hold momentum.
rows.needed: Protected time for key SMEs against BAU and acknowledgement of slowed current work.
rows.implication: A single unavailable SME can move the critical path.

rows.working_through: Backlog readiness for the first PI: the initial ART backlog is not yet refined into PI-ready Features.
rows.doing_done: Running the Jira backlog review; applying a Definition of Ready to refine work into PI-ready Features ahead of planning.
rows.needed: Backing to protect refinement time before PI Planning.
rows.implication: PI Planning becomes a refinement exercise rather than a planning event.

decisions.title: Leadership Decisions Needed For Pilot Effectiveness
decisions.subtitle: Each key risk resolves to a specific ask or decision leadership must make to maximize pilot effectiveness

rows.risk: Dedicated pilot capacity cannot be protected. Launching the five-team Connectivity pilot requires reallocating existing resources from active initiatives.
rows.ask: Endorse the proposed five-team pilot staffing approach and accept that selected in-flight initiatives may be re-sequenced or deferred while the pilot is validated.

rows.risk: Current strategic initiatives may experience delivery impacts (e.g., Data Center Exits, Starburst & Colorless, BPI Migration).
rows.ask: Confirm which initiatives should absorb reduced capacity, be re-sequenced, or be deferred (initial list provided; holistic assessment underway).

rows.risk: The pilot requires an interim funding approach. A value stream cannot operate effectively through project-based funding alone.
rows.ask: Approve an interim value stream funding approach while the long-term model is finalized (with Finance, Pod E).

rows.risk: Workforce transitions require cross-functional alignment. Named resources span multiple organizations and people managers.
rows.ask: Align functional leaders on resource transitions and release timing for dedicated pilot staffing.

rows.risk: End-to-end transformation may exceed current scope. The model primarily addresses software delivery; upstream intake and pre-ART activities require further design.
rows.ask: Endorse continued development of the upstream engagement model across Network A&E, upstream intake, and pre-ART activities.

main_tables.title: Protecting Pilot Capacity Creates Real Tradeoffs
main_tables.subtitle: Initial view of current initiatives that may be affected by dedicating resources to the pilot; final impacts confirmed as assignments are validated
rows: Apigee shutdown and mid-cutover activities require sustained delivery capacity; redirecting key resources may delay delivery and increase outage risk.
Finalize workforce assignments and confirm delivery sequencing with functional leaders before pilot staffing is finalized.
Supports significant customer commitments with major revenue implications; redirecting engineering capacity may impact timelines and contractual commitments.
Foundational to broader IT modernization; resource transitions may slow key transformation milestones.
Assess impact as workforce mapping completes.
Scarce architecture and design capacity may be redirected to the pilot, slowing lower-priority design requests across the portfolio.
Confirm dedicated Network A&E capacity and reprioritize remaining demand through portfolio governance.

appendix.title: Pod-Level Workplan Detail
appendix.subtitle: Next steps by pod for the week ahead
bullets: Pod A (People & Change): socialize comms plan, finish capacity & skill-gap assessment, finalize training approach, develop manager guides.
Pod B (Strategy & Governance): finalize governance framework, PM principles, SDLC, and success metrics; assign decision rights with Pod C.
Pod C (Value Stream Design): finalize names-in-boxes, review backlog readiness, define transition into Q4 PI Planning.
Pod D (Architecture & Delivery): stand up Jira/SharePoint hierarchy, complete API and dependency mapping, define governance cadence.
Pod E (Funding & Metrics): finalize funding decisions with Finance, draft value-stream funding model, define pilot KPIs.
